newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sixt plans convert non-voting pref shares.
newsitem.headline: Sixt plans convert non-voting pref shares.

text.p: German car rental company Sixt AG said on Monday it planned to convert its non-voting preference shares into ordinary common shares.
In a mandatory statement, the company also said it planned to reduce the nominal value of its shares to five marks from 50 marks.
Sixt also said it would pay a 14 mark dividend on ordinary shares for 1996, unchanged from the year before, but that it would also pay a 3.50 mark bonus.
Preference share holders, who will receive a 15 mark dividend, are also to receive the 3.50 mark bonus, Sixt said.
